# Contract-First API Design

**Write the API specification first; generate the code from it.** The inverse — annotate the
controllers and let a tool emit a spec afterwards — produces a document that describes whatever the
code happens to do, which cannot be a contract because it can never disagree with the
implementation.

Contract-first makes the spec the artefact that other parties agree to, and makes drift a *compile
error* rather than a documentation problem: if the handwritten class stops matching the generated
interface, the build fails.

## As implemented in lab 2

`lab2/StudentService/` in [[information-systems-modelling]] is the whole point of the lab:

- An OpenAPI YAML document is the source. `openapi-generator-maven-plugin` 7.20.0 runs it at build
  time into `target/generated-sources/openapi`, wired onto the compile path by
  `build-helper-maven-plugin` — see [[maven]].
- **`interfaceOnly` + `delegatePattern`.** The generator emits only interfaces and a delegate
  seam; no controller body is generated, so regeneration never overwrites hand-written logic. This is
  the configuration that makes the pattern survive contact with a real codebase — the naive
  full-generation mode makes the generated tree unmergeable and the pattern gets abandoned.
- `springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui` serves Swagger UI over the running app, so the contract is
  browsable rather than a file someone has to find.
- Persistence via [[sqlite]] behind a [[layered-architecture]] split, on [[spring-boot]].

Four OpenAPI `.yaml` documents exist across the repo — the contract is carried forward with the rest
of each lab under [[forward-copy-lab-progression]].

## Where it sits in the SDLC arc

The repo runs one invented domain through requirements → contract → implementation → ontology →
publishing → process models. Contract-first is the hinge between the prose requirements of lab 1 and
the executable artefacts after it: the SRS says what the system must do, the OpenAPI document says
exactly what the wire looks like, and only then is any Java written.

The same instinct — hold the definition once, derive everything else — reappears as
[[single-source-of-truth-generators]] in labs 6 and 7, and as
[[generate-markup-instead-of-hand-writing-it]]. This repo applies it to APIs, to RDF markup and to
BPMN diagrams, in three different technologies.

## Limits observed

- **TODO:** no requirement identifier from the lab 1 SRS is cited by any endpoint, schema or process
  model. The link from requirements to contract is narrative only — there is no traceability matrix
  in any format. `confidence: low` on any claim that the contract demonstrably satisfies the SRS.
- The generated tree lives in `target/`, which inflated a naive source-file count of this repo from
  134 to 231. Generated code being indistinguishable from source at a glance is a real cost of the
  pattern.
